title: Stabilization of dark states in emitter arrays coupled to a half-waveguide
authors: Oriol Rubies-Bigorda, Susanne F. Yelin, Ana Asenjo-Garcia, Stuart J. Masson
abstract: The radiative properties of quantum emitters are profoundly influenced by their electromagnetic environment. When coupled to a waveguide terminated at one end by a mirror, distant emitters interact strongly via virtual photon exchange, leading to collective superradiant and subradiant states with enhanced or suppressed decay rates. We demonstrate that applying optimal frequency shifts to each emitter enables the formation of perfect single-excitation dark states (i.e. states with zero decay rate) and near-perfect multi-excitation dark states in small ensembles. These collective states can be deterministically prepared with high fidelity using classical driving fields or few-photon pulses propagating along the waveguide. These results, readily implementable in superconducting qubit platforms, open new avenues for quantum information storage, networking and control of light.
summary: This paper details the theoretical control of collective quantum states in arrays of emitters coupled to a waveguide. By applying precise frequency shifts, the authors demonstrate how to engineer perfect single-excitation dark states that are immune to decay. This technique is crucial for building robust quantum information storage and networking devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is stabilizing perfect single-excitation and near-perfect multi-excitation dark states in arrays of quantum emitters coupled to a waveguide.
main_result: Optimal frequency shifts allow for the deterministic preparation of single-excitation dark states, and near-perfect multi-excitation dark states can be achieved by treating the system as coupled subsystems.
method: The analysis uses the master equation and Hamiltonian diagonalization to find states that decouple from the dissipative environment, requiring precise tuning of emitter detunings.
model_or_system: The system consists of N two-level emitters (qubits) coupled to a one-dimensional photonic waveguide terminated by a mirror. Dynamics are governed by a Lindbladian evolution incorporating coherent and dissipative couplings.
key_observables: Dark state population ($p_D$), decay rate ($\gamma$), and the error ($\epsilon$) in state preparation.
important_parameters: Optimal relative detuning ($\Delta_{opt}$), number of emitters ($N$), and the strength of external driving fields ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The Markov approximation is used, and for some analyses, adiabatic elimination is employed under the assumption that driving fields are weak compared to decay rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the array setup, the decay paths in the Lindbladian spectrum, and the error ($\epsilon$) in photon emission for two-emitter systems under noise.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general theory of dark states in coupled emitters, detailing the stabilization mechanism for single excitations via detuning, generalizing to multi-excitations, and finally analyzing the robustness of the preparation protocol against noise.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses controlling dissipation in open quantum systems, which is central to quantum memory and quantum networking using solid-state emitters.
